_comment: Ledger of recurring prose habits (constructions, gestures, paragraph/scene closers), the language-level counterpart to motifs.json. Nightly sessions read this before drafting and add entries after. Status: 'develop' = use only in a new form; 'rest' = do not use until rested_until chapter; 'watch' = fine in moderation. Saturday review prunes and logs counts.

constructions.pattern: 'the way [clause]' used as a trailing simile
constructions.example: the way you feel an old break in the weather before you feel the ache of it
constructions.note: Came off rest at ch. 12 as scheduled. Draft reached for it five times before revision; four were cut back to plain statements or a different image, leaving one clean use (Vail's delight echoing an old teaching memory). Confirms the instinct to overreach for it the moment it's available again — keep trimming hard rather than letting it regrow to ch. 7-9 levels.

constructions.example: a thing to explain; a thing your body has quietly decided
constructions.note: Off rest at ch. 12 and still clean at zero — third chapter running without it. Name the actual object or action.

constructions.pattern: 'I have learned/found/never...' followed by a general rule
constructions.example: I have learned the exact weight a thing has to reach before it's worth the cost of saying it out loud
constructions.note: Lloyd's self-knowledge should show up as behaviour, not as narrated wisdom. Clean through ch. 12 as well, without needing to reach for it — the confession-retelling format gave Lloyd plenty to react to without summarising himself.

Ch. 12 held the established range. The long/short contrast moved to a new pairing this chapter: Lloyd's long waiting-and-rumination sentences against Maria's own looping compound sentences when she retells the confession, rather than against clipped procedural dialogue (ch. 10-11's version). Same habit, new partner — keep rotating what the long sentences are set against rather than defaulting to the procedural-dialogue contrast every time.

constructions.pattern: 'same as [clause]' used as a trailing comparison, the direct replacement for the rested the-way-simile
constructions.example: same as I run all of them back now
constructions.note: Clean at zero again in ch. 12 — draft reached for it twice (the building's breathing, Vail's bread-baking) and both were rewritten to plainer statements. Two chapters clean; it isn't hardening into a habit.

constructions.pattern: Lloyd narrates his own perception-management in filing/accounting/procedural language
constructions.example: filed and closed and not brought up again; I did the sum; running the frame back
constructions.note: Clean for a second chapter running. Ch. 12 gave Edie the ledger and the ledger-language instead (totting, pricing, assessing) and kept Lloyd's own interiority physical — the hand, the elbow, the weighed stone — rather than clerical. Treat as staying evolved away from unless it resurfaces.

constructions.pattern: a clause restated through its own negation for flat understatement — 'didn't X because there wasn't X to do', 'wasn't an answer that wasn't Y'
constructions.example: she didn't say anything useful, because there wasn't anything useful to say; I didn't have an answer that wasn't the same thing said back to her, worse
constructions.note: Did not recur in ch. 12 — confirms it was a one-chapter cluster rather than a hardening tic. Safe to use again if it arises naturally, but don't reach for it as a default.

constructions.pattern: a statement capped with a trailing 'which was/is [flat judgment]' clause
constructions.example: which was true, and also the kindest thing she could have said to her just then; which was as much of a question as Edie generally asks
constructions.note: New this chapter — four uses. Reads naturally as Lloyd's habit of appending a dry verdict to something he's just reported rather than editorialising mid-sentence, but four in one chapter is a cluster. Watch for ch. 13: if it repeats unchanged, it needs developing into a new shape rather than reuse.

closers.pattern: paragraph or chapter ends on the narrator stating what he did not say, or what the scene means
closers.example: I said none of that. I hadn't said anything since the school wall and didn't start now.
closers.note: End on an action, an object or a line of dialogue. Ch. 12 closed on Edie's cord going still in her hands instead — an object, not an explanation.
